# spacequery

Observe-only view of one developer's machine for coding agents: agents, dirty repos, worktrees, sessions, and related occupancy. Each call builds a fresh in-memory SQLite database from providers, prints rows, and exits. It does not mutate providers.

Use it before editing, starting servers, opening PRs, or taking over old work, so the agent knows who and what already occupies the machine.

Agent skill: [skills/spacequery/SKILL.md](skills/spacequery/SKILL.md)

Installed package: `node_modules/spacequery/skills/spacequery/SKILL.md` (this file at `node_modules/spacequery/llms.txt`).

## Commands

- `spacequery <query|report>` — run a named catalog query or report
- `spacequery --sql <text>` — ad hoc SQL over the in-memory DB
- `spacequery watch <query> --until <predicate>` — re-run one named query until the current rows match
- `spacequery --help` — the short query list; `--help --all` lists every enabled query; `--help --json` is that list as data
- `spacequery doctor` — report whether each enabled built-in provider answered (`spacequery doctor --json` is the same JSON)
- `spacequery ui` — terminal browser for tables, queries, and reports. Reports renders the same section list as the CLI.
- Common flags: `--root`, `--scope root|agents|all`, `--me`, `--json` / `--tsv`, `--trace`, `--expect-empty`, `--strict`

Named queries include `here`-style occupancy via catalog entries such as `in-dir`, `dirty`, `sessions`, `agents-with-sessions`, `worktrees` (see `--help`). `issues-in-scope` and `issues-ready` list open and claimable beads issues and default to `--scope all`. `work` shows that list with herdr and local Cursor agent models. Its definition is `dashboard.ts`; `spacequery work --json` repeats it as `definition`. Edit that file to change the sections, then run `spacequery work` again. Incomplete observation is explicit in the result. Before you assume empty means none, run `spacequery doctor` if providers look incomplete. Prefer narrowing scope over guessing from a partial view.

## Doctor

`spacequery doctor` loads every enabled built-in provider once on one root and prints JSON. `--json` selects that same document. `--root` defaults to the git toplevel of the current directory. Doctor does not take `--scope`, does not install tools, and does not run user-provider commands. `beads`, `brew`, `headsign`, and `runtag` are off until config enables them. Doctor lists those names in `disabled_providers`.

Read the report's `ok`, then each provider's `ok` and `error`. `path` counts PATH entries, missing entries, and duplicates when the search path provider answered. `user_providers.present` is 1 when the user-provider directory exists. Exit 0 means the report was printed. When doctor itself cannot run, stdout is an `error` and a `do` command, with no stack.

## Watch

`spacequery watch <query> --until <predicate>` re-runs a named query. Each tick builds a fresh database. `--until` is required. Watch does not store rows and does not write to a provider.

Predicates:

- `empty` — zero rows
- `nonempty` — one or more rows
- `<column>=<value>` or `<column>=<a>|<b>` — every current row has that column set to one of the values. Zero rows do not match. Null does not match.

An incomplete observation (a provider with `ok` 0) does not satisfy `--until`. Empty rows beside a failed provider stay unknown.

```sh
spacequery watch in-dir --until empty
spacequery watch working --until empty
spacequery watch in-dir --until agent_status=idle|blocked
spacequery watch claude-sessions --until status=idle
spacequery watch runs-in-dir --root <repo> --until status=exited
```

`agent_status` on `in-dir`, `working`, and `agents` is `working`, `idle`, `blocked`, or `unknown`. `working` only returns agents that are working, so wait with `--until empty`. `claude-sessions` has `status`. `runs-in-dir` has `status` from a runtag job file: `running` or `exited`.

[runtag](https://github.com/meganemura/runtag) ([npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/runtag)) records the job. [spacequery](https://github.com/meganemura/spacequery) ([npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/spacequery)) reads the file and watches. Install runtag with `npm i -g runtag`. Record with `runtag exec --detach --cwd <repo> -- <cmd>...`, wait with `spacequery watch runs-in-dir --root <repo> --until status=exited`, then read `exit_code` with `runtag status <id>`. spacequery reads `$XDG_DATA_HOME/runtag/jobs/<id>.json` (default `~/.local/share/runtag/jobs/`). A job that still says `running` after its supervisor pid died stays `running` with `orphan` 1 and `exit_code` null, and does not satisfy `status=exited`. A missing jobs directory is an empty answer (`runtag` `ok` 1). Doctor reports the same: unreadable jobs directory or an unparsable job file is `ok` 0.

`--interval` defaults to 2000 milliseconds. `--timeout` defaults to 300 seconds. `--timeout 0` waits until the predicate or a signal.

The first snapshot prints immediately. Later snapshots print only when the observation changes. JSON from watch is one envelope per line (NDJSON). One-shot JSON stays indented.

Exit 0 when `--until` matches. Exit 5 when `--timeout` elapses first; the last snapshot is already printed. Exit 130 on SIGINT or SIGTERM. `--strict` still exits 4 when a provider did not answer. `--expect-empty` still exits 3 when the matching snapshot has rows.
